extracted.intended_audience: school and postsecondary administrators, Title IX coordinators, disability services officers, legal counsel, and stakeholders participating in Title IX rulemaking or compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal standards for recipients of Federal financial assistance on implementing and complying with the Department's final Title IX regulations, and the Department's explanations of rulemaking procedures and supporting regulatory analyses. Covers intersections with disability laws, training, evidence disclosure, consultation requirements, and procedural/analytic obligations for the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with disability laws in Title IX processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with obligations under disability laws (e.g., Title II/III/ADA, IDEA) with respect to students, employees, or participants in a Title IX reporting or grievance process situation, regardless of the recipient's internal organizational structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These final regulations concerning sexual harassment do not address a recipient's obligations under the ADA and do not preclude notifying students about rights to disability accommodations. Recipients must comply with disability laws across intake, written communications with complainants and respondents, review of evidence (§106.45(b)(5)(vi)), and holding live hearings (including separate rooms or virtual hearings under §106.45(b)(6)(i)). The Department will offer technical assistance on complying with overlapping obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of identities under §106.71(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must keep confidential the identity of any individual who has made a report or complaint of sex discrimination, any complainant, any individual reported to be the perpetrator, any respondent, and any witness, except as permitted by FERPA, required by law, or as necessary to conduct the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This confidentiality requirement coexists with obligations under disability laws; where disability laws require disclosure (e.g., to allow a support person), recipients must reconcile these duties within the exceptions stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support person accommodations for persons with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Apart from an advisor of choice under §106.45(b)(5)(iv), recipients must comply with any disability laws that require permitting a support person to accompany a person with a disability during a grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus a recipient may be required under disability laws to permit a person with a disability to be accompanied throughout a grievance process by a support person in addition to the party's advisor of choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmative inquiry about disability accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may, and nothing in the final regulations precludes them from, affirmatively inquiring of each party whether any disability accommodation is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If accommodations are requested or required, recipients must comply with applicable legal obligations under disability laws, including obligations such as IDEA Child Find where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conflicts of interest for Title IX roles
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(1)(iii) prohibits conflicts of interest on the part of Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, or those who facilitate informal resolution processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a Title IX Coordinator also serving as an ADA compliance officer presents a prohibited conflict is fact-specific; the Department declines to categorically prohibit dual roles and will offer technical assistance regarding compliance and conflict determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on impartiality and avoiding bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Training for covered personnel must include how to serve impartially, including by avoiding prejudgment of the facts at issue, conflicts of interest, and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised §106.45(b)(1)(iii) to explicitly include this language in required training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence disclosure format requirement (§106.45(b)(5)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must send to each party and the party's advisor, if any, the evidence subject to inspection and review in an electronic format or a hard copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department removed the NPRM reference to a file-sharing platform; recipients must provide accessible electronic or hard-copy evidence to parties and advisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: No regulatory obligation to require demographic data collection/analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to impose, in these final regulations, an obligation on recipients to collect and analyze data on complainants and respondents (e.g., by disability, race, sexual identity) for purposes of assessing disproportionate outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Department acknowledges such self-study can be valuable and recipients may voluntarily undertake it, it is not required by these final regulations; recipients remain free to collect data at their discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency is not required to post all received comments before close of comment period
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department did not commit to electronically posting all public comments it received before the comment period ended, and there is no legal requirement to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACUS recommendation encourages posting 'to the extent possible,' but agencies need time to process comments before posting; the Department posted comments as expeditiously as possible and provided other avenues for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and nondiscrimination in review of public comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department reviewed and considered comments submitted by any person regardless of race, class, educational status, ability status, dialects or vernaculars, or level of legal sophistication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns about the functionality of regulations.gov or technical outages do not change the Department's obligation to review comments; the NPRM was available through multiple websites during the public comment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant Attorney General review for Executive Order 12250
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department complied with Executive Order 12250 by having the Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights review the proposed rules and approve the NPRM for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This satisfies the commenters' assertion that DOJ approval was required prior to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBA Advocacy and small entity consultation threshold (5 U.S.C. 609(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: SBA Advocacy review is appropriate, but 5 U.S.C. 609(a) (special techniques to assure small entity participation) applies only if a rule has a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities; the Department certified this rule does not have such an impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if §609(a) applied, one technique is publishing proposed rules in publications likely to be obtained by small entities; the Department published the NPRM in the Federal Register and provided opportunities to comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal consultation policy application
rubrics_metrics.description: Section IV of the Department's Consultation and Coordination with American Indian and Alaska Native Tribal Governments policy requires tribal consultation for actions that have a substantial and direct effect on tribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because these Title IX regulations affect students broadly and do not target tribes specifically, the Department treated tribes the same as other stakeholders and concluded special tribal consultation beyond normal outreach was not required; nevertheless tribes had the same opportunity to comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with Bureau of Indian Affairs Part 42 due process protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Bureau-funded schools have due process protections that exceed these final regulations, those additional protections do not contradict these final regulations and a Bureau-funded school may comply with both sets of requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The existence of more protective rules for Bureau-funded schools does not create a direct conflict with the Title IX final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13132 (federalism) applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: EO 13132's consultation and federalism requirements may not apply where a regulation is a condition of receiving federal funds and recipients may forgo funds if they do not wish to comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if EO 13132 were applicable, the Department addressed State and local official comments and issued a federalism summary impact statement; the Order does not prescribe specific consultation methods such as newsletters or listservs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency and reproducibility of Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NPRM's RIA must provide sufficient specificity (formulas, methods, references to underlying public data) to allow others to reproduce the analysis and test conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department explains that underlying documents reviewed were publicly available, that assumptions and coding choices were explained, and alternative impact analyses were provided (e.g., sensitivity analyses) when coding choices could vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of available national data sources (Clery Act, CRDC) in regulatory analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department used the most appropriate and available data (Clery Act, CRDC, Subcommittee report, IPEDS) to inform its analyses and invited commenters to suggest alternative data sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department is not aware of a more reliable comprehensive data source and used comparisons across data sources to inform estimates (e.g., number of investigations); commenters were able to challenge assumptions or provide alternatives during the comment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Executive Order 13771 when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Where revisions to the proposed regulations change the applicability of EO 13771 (reducing regulatory costs), the Department will apply EO 13771 and provide revised economic analysis in the Regulatory Impact Analysis section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department concluded EO 13771 applies to these final regulations and updated its analysis accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of distributional effects analysis in RIA
rubrics_metrics.description: The RIA analyzed impacts across types of institutions (e.g., two-year vs four-year, large vs small institutions) but did not quantify distributional effects across student demographic groups for the cost-benefit analysis of the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department explains the NPRM's RIA focused on economic effects of the proposed regulations and treated students equally across demographic categories for that purpose; commenters' requests to analyze distributional effects by demographic groups were not adopted into the economic analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiated rulemaking under HEA §492 not required for Title IX
rubrics_metrics.description: The negotiated rulemaking requirement in section 492 of the HEA applies only to regulations that implement provisions of Title IV of the HEA and does not apply to Title IX regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Title IX is not part of Title IV (student financial aid programs), the Department was not required to undertake negotiated rulemaking for these Title IX final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IV master calendar requirement inapplicable to Title IX
rubrics_metrics.description: The HEA master calendar requirement (that certain Title IV regulatory changes published after Nov. 1 become effective in the second award year) applies exclusively to rules affecting Title IV programs and does not apply to Title IX regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Title IX regulations may impact institutions that participate in Title IV, they are not 'program[s] under Title IV' and thus the master calendar timing does not constrain effective dates for these Title IX rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency coordination via OMB review satisfies coordination obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordination with other agencies and efforts to reduce regulatory inconsistencies were accomplished by sharing the proposed regulations with the Office of Management and Budget prior to publication, allowing agencies the opportunity to review and comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB interagency review is the mechanism used to promote coordination and avoid inconsistent, incompatible, or duplicative regulations among agencies that enforce Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: APA requirement to disclose basis and provide reasoned explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: To withstand judicial review under the Administrative Procedure Act, an agency must disclose the basis of its action and provide a reasoned explanation for departures from past practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department states it has provided the basis for the regulatory changes in the NPRM and these final regulations (including adoption/adaptation of the Supreme Court's framework to address sexual harassment) and denies that the rulemaking was undertaken in bad faith or for a pretextual rationale.
